forecasts.reason: Theory: odd k removes the 2-2 ties that even k breaks by sample order, so vote over 9 should sit at or a little above the preliminary even-k vote over 8 (458); the theory's 'plateau near 453' pulls the centre down, while the preliminary vote over 12 (466) pushes the top of the interval up.

Theory: at even k ties are settled by sample order, and on hard328 most ties are between wrong singletons, so going from 4 to 8 samples lifts the base above its vote over 4 (192) by less than its pass@4 (207) would allow.

Theory: M(2) has few cap hits, so lone right answers face finished wrong singletons; at even k=4 the 2-2 and 1-1-1-1 ties that k=3 avoided come back and are lost about half the time, so the vote stays at or just below its vote over 3 (246) rather than climbing toward pass@4.

Theory: at the 32k cap, answers that abstained at 16k become finished wrong singletons, and tied lone right answers lose about half the time, so most of the single-sample gain from finishing is lost in the vote: only a small rise over 75, as on hard328 (238 to 244).
